correctness.rationale: In the homogeneous Fano-free 3-hypergraph, every new point is encoded by a graph on old pair coordinates. A Fano copy containing that point is equivalent to a Pasch on old points with all three opposite-pair coordinates selected. Partial Steiner uniqueness forces distinct Pasches to share at most one opposite pair; sharing one entails no further shared old vertex and therefore at least ten old vertices. Inclusion-exclusion yields admissible fractions 7/8, 25/32 or 49/64, and any third distinct forbidden triple has a strictly additional witness. The explicit 6-, 10-, and 12-vertex examples satisfy old-base constraints and attain the bounds. The included standalone verifier independently implements full Fano 7-line embeddings, the Pasch signature, direct link counts and local finite witnesses; these finite checks are distinct from the universal proof.

value.rationale: The Pasch is the unique six-point Fano deletion, so its detection directly determines the first obstruction to one-point type freedom. The theorem identifies two sharp successive universal loss factors with rigid equality and an exact ten-point first attainment threshold; this distinguishes nontrivial local geometry of parameter designs rather than computing an arbitrary isolated invariant. All PSTS parameter bases are covered, with explicit structural obstructions to generalizing the equality condition.
